findings:
🟠 [blg-skip-cross-style] MUST-FIX: In scripts/check-backlog-entries.js, table mode (collectEntries→parseTable) never examines non-`|` lines, and checklist mode (parseChecklist) drops a `### ` boundary line and silently overwrites the previous item's fields when a foreign-style entry follows valid entries — concretely, a heading-style entry appended to a table- or checklist-declared BACKLOG.md produces zero violations and exit 0, so the gate reports clean while the row is invisible to field checks, the 900 B entry cap, and the allowlist fingerprint (the spec pre-declares "a block silently skipped = defect"; heading mode already handles this via the orphan→unparseable heuristic). Smallest remediation: in the table and checklist branches, flag entry-shaped non-conforming lines (lines matching `^\s*###\s` or `- **Field**:` / `- Field:` bullets outside the declared grammar) as `unparseable_entry`, reusing the heading-mode orphan heuristic, plus two --self-test cases covering each branch.
🔵 [blg-sechdr-fp] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: heading mode appends a mid-file `## Section` header to the previous `###` block and fires extra_content (fieldLine null → extra). Fail-loud, and references/backlog-entry.md defines entries as `###` blocks with prose only as preamble; excluded unless a real backlog file is shown to use `##` sections — remediation if needed: treat `^##\s` as a block boundary without orphan-flush.
🔵 [blg-test-exec-bit] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: new hooks/tests/check-backlog-entries.test.sh is mode 100644 while sibling suites (resolve-project-paths.test.sh is 100755) carry the exec bit; if the runner executes suites directly the red-first suite silently never runs. The runner's invocation style is not visible in the diff, so verify it and `chmod +x` (one bit) rather than block this version.
🔵 [blg-scaffold-detect] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: detectBacklogStyle in scripts/scaffold-config.js inspects only the first non-empty line, so a table backlog with an h1 title or any checklist backlog scaffolds `style: heading`; the gate then fails loud (orphan/unparseable), not silent, and the generated config invites editing — Phase 4 hardening, excluded from Phases 1–3.
🔵 [blg-caps-case] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: parseConfigFile's first cap regex is case-insensitive (`caps\.(\w+)`), so `- caps.title: 80` is stored lowercase and then silently ignored by effectiveCap/checkCapsRaised, which key on the canonical `Title`; both templates document the canonical form — normalize the captured key to the canonical field name or emit a config error.
🔵 [blg-selftest-deadcode] CUT/FOLLOW-UP: runSelfTest computes an unused `hit` binding and duplicates the `unseen` check as an inline loop; dead code with no behavioral effect — cosmetic cleanup excluded from this version.
